reference_diagnosis.name: Dopa-responsive dystonia, GCH1-related, adult-onset parkinsonism phenotype
reference_diagnosis.basis: Slowly progressive asymmetric parkinsonism with foot dystonia, sustained low-dose levodopa response for years without fluctuations or dyskinesia, normal DAT-SPECT, GCH1 variant.

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Levodopa-responsive asymmetric parkinsonism, foot dystonia common in PRKN
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: DaT-SPECT normal (held out); no fluctuations after 4 years at low dose is atypical but not exclusionary for PRKN, so imaging is key

key_evidence_gaps.question: DaT-SPECT never done
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: The key discriminator between DRD and PD

key_evidence_gaps.question: Off-medication examination and diurnal assessment
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Classical DRD features may be masked by treatment

held_out_evidence.result: Heterozygous pathogenic GCH1 variant; PRKN/PINK1 negative.
Moderate right-sided bradykinesia and right foot dystonia; mild improvement noted by patient after nap.

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Accepting PD because of levodopa response alone
Concluding 'no DRD' because classic clues (diurnal, family history, childhood onset) are absent
Recommending changes to the patient's levodopa dose
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
clinician_review_notes: DRAFT. Wiki to check clinical plausibility, findings, held-out results, and red flags.
